votes.reason: As the largest XLF bank it is the most direct expression of my Financials call (a +45 bp steepening curve, the Fed on hold and Basel III capital relief), and it sits at 99.6% of its high with XLF near $57.60; the risk of payrolls under 50K belongs to the sector call itself, not to this name.

Its +16% earnings week is part of the breadth my Healthcare thesis cites, and as a biotech that moves on its own news it gives the low correlation to SPY the sector is meant to add before Friday's jobs report, with little direct exposure to LLY's Aug 6 swing.

It is the kind of large multinational my Staples call names: a dollar below 100 and cheaper oil-linked inputs help it, it is at a 52-week closing high while XLP draws inflows, and it is the hedge for Friday's jobs report my call asks for.

It fits my Financials call because a steeper curve lifts the yield on reinvested client cash and the Basel III capital relief reaches its bank, and it is at its 52-week high alongside XLF; it adds more of the same payrolls risk rather than a new one.

It sits in my Healthcare call, where managed care adds the low-correlation ballast the sector is there for with less exposure to LLY's Aug 6 report; its 26% EPS decline is a stock-picking concern that the 10% weight already reflects, not a problem with sector fit.
